problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $\frac{3}{2}\,\text{kg}$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2},$
where $x$ and $y$ are measured in meters.
Find the moment of inertia of the plate about a line perpendicular to $D$ at a distance of $\sqrt{6}\,\text{m}$ from a parallel line passing through its center of mass.

feedback.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $\frac{6}{5}\,\text{kg}$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,-3\le y\le 3},$
where $x$ and $y$ are measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about a line perpendicular to $D$ at a distance of $\sqrt{5}\,\text{m}$ from a parallel line passing through its center of mass.
feedback.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina of mass $M$ and a line ${l}_{M}$ perpendicular to the lamina passing through its center of mass, the parallel axis theorem states that the moment of inertia of the lamina about a line $l$ parallel to ${l}_{M}$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M,
$$

where $d$ is the distance between the lines, and ${I}_{M}$ and ${I}_{l}$ are the moments of inertia about the lines ${l}_{M}$ and $l,$ respectively.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=2\cdot 6=12\,{\text{m}}^{2}.$
Since the plate has a uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{(\frac{6}{5})}{12}=\frac{1}{10}\,\text{kg}/{\text{m}}^{2},
$$

and its center of mass is its centroid:

$$
(\overset{¯}{x},\overset{¯}{y})=(\frac{-1+1}{2},\frac{-3+3}{2})=(0,0)
$$

Since the center of mass is at the origin, the moment of inertia about the perpendicular line through the center of mass is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{M} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{3}\frac{1}{10}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{10}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{[{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{y=-3}^{y=3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{10}{\int }_{-1}^{1}6{x}^{2}+18\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{10}{[2{x}^{3}+18x]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(4+36) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot 40 \\  & =4\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about a line $\sqrt{5}\,\text{m}$ from the center of mass is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M \\  & =4+(\sqrt{5})^{2}\cdot \frac{6}{5} \\  & =4+6 \\  & =10\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
